# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Weekly Report (May 10 - 16, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, development focused heavily on stabilizing the testing suite and refining core interoperability components. Significant effort was directed toward resolving persistent flaky tests in the CI/CD pipeline, particularly those involving reorg recovery and withdrawal proving. Key progress was made on the Interop Proofs Devnet roadmap, alongside critical updates to client library withdrawal logic to ensure compatibility with timestamp-based proving. Routine maintenance also continued with multiple automated codegen updates to keep the registry synchronized.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Automated Registry Maintenance
The team maintained the registry's consistency through regular automated updates.
*   **Codegen Updates:** Two pull requests ([#1225](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1225) and [#1226](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1226)) were opened to handle automated code generation, ensuring that the registry remains current with upstream changes and generated data structures.

### Interoperability & Protocol Refinement
Work continued on the foundational elements of the Superchain's interoperability layer.
*   **Interop Proofs Devnet:** The "Definition of Done" for the Interop Proofs Devnet ([#20489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20489)) was formalized, establishing clear milestones for superdispute games, flashblocks, and conductor re-orgs.
*   **Message Validation:** A new implementation strategy for unsafe head executing message validation was proposed, linked to work in the broader Optimism repository ([#20650](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20650)).
*   **Withdrawal Proving Logic:** To improve the reliability of withdrawals, progress was made on transitioning client libraries to use timestamps instead of block numbers when proving withdrawals ([#18614](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/18614)), supported by an upstream PR in the Viem library.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **`op-supernode` Reporting:** Investigation into `op-supernode`'s `RequiredL1` reporting ([#20657](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20657)) concluded that the system is functioning as intended. The reported divergence between Challenger and Kona was identified as a test-setup artifact rather than a protocol bug, confirming that `RequiredL1` correctly tracks local-safe-derivation.

### New & Active Issues (Flaky Test Mitigation)
The primary focus of active issue management this week was the stabilization of the test suite, which has seen several recurring failures:
*   **Reorg and Sync Flakes:** Root cause analyses were conducted for `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterSafeReorg` ([#19884](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19884)) and `TestFollowL2_ReorgRecovery` ([#19967](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19967)), leading to fixes in PRs #20651 and #20652.
*   **Withdrawal Timing Issues:** `TestWithdrawal_Cannon` ([#19963](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19963)) was reopened due to a failure mode where gas estimation occurred before the dispute game was technically active. A draft fix ([#20677](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20677)) is in progress to ensure the L1 head time exceeds the game creation time before retrying proofs.
*   **Persistent Sync Issues:** `TestELSyncSafeRetractedByOffset` ([#20334](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20334)) remains a blocker; despite 120 retry attempts, the test continues to fail, suggesting a deep-seated timing bug in the execution layer synchronization.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by tight coordination between the registry maintainers and upstream library developers. The work on withdrawal proving necessitated a cross-project contribution to the **Viem** library, demonstrating the project's role in influencing the broader Ethereum developer tooling ecosystem. Internal collaboration was also high regarding the "Definition of Done" for the Interop Devnet, involving coordination across the proofs, flashblocks, and conductor teams to align on success criteria for the upcoming network deployment.
